ME3600 control demos

Real-time simulations from the course. No MATLAB needed: pick an example, type your controller C(s) and test it.

Routh Hurwitz

Same sims as the MATLAB Realtime demos: type C(s), watch the closed loop, read the closed-loop poles.

  • DC Motor ServoThe shaft follows a commanded angle that changes every 2 s.
  • Car Lane ChangeThe car drives at constant speed and changes lane every 8 s. The controller steers the front wheels.
  • Cold Storage RoomThe AC cools the room to a temperature that changes every 6 s. It can only cool, so P ≥ 0.
  • Inverted PendulumKeep the pendulum upright. It starts tilted by 5°; push it to test the controller.
  • Mass Spring DamperA force u moves the mass to a target position that changes every 4 s.
  • Damped PendulumThe pendulum hangs from a pivot and is driven to a commanded angle that changes every 4 s.
  • Satellite AttitudeThrusters turn the satellite to an orientation that changes every 6 s. No friction, no gravity.
  • Two-Mass SystemA force on mass 1 moves it to a commanded position; mass 2 swings on the spring between them.
  • Water Tank LevelThe inflow fills the tank to a level that changes every 20 s. The tank is drawn to scale. Try 5× speed.
  • Ball on PlateKeep the ball on the green target by tilting the plate yourself, then hand it to C(s). The same controller acts on the x and y axes.
  • Highwire ArtistThe artist stands on the wire and balances with a pole. Try it yourself, then hand it to C(s).
  • Cart PendulumKeep the pendulum upright by pushing the cart. Try it yourself, then hand it to C(s). The view follows the cart.

Frequency Response

Chapter 7 demos: what a linear system does to a sinusoid, and a song played through G(s).

  • Servo Frequency ResponseA sinusoidal voltage drives the motor. At low frequency the speed follows (×K, in phase); above the corner 1/τ it shrinks and lags by up to 90°.
  • Spring-Damper Frequency ResponseYou move the end of a damper; a spring holds the plate. Slow motion: the damper slides and the plate stays (high-pass). Fast motion: the damper acts like a rod and the plate follows.
  • Resonance DemoA sinusoidal force pushes the mass. Slow forcing: the mass follows the dashed block (F/k). Near ωn: resonance. Fast forcing: the mass barely moves, opposite to the force.
  • The Muffled SongHear a Bode plot. A jungle track plays in a loop through G(s). Lower the corner frequency and the hats and cymbals fade while the bass stays: the song sounds as if behind a wall.
